body:
```text
4) CONCALL TRUTH-TRACKER
From the last 8 concall transcripts, tabulate every quantitative guidance
statement (revenue, margin, capex, capacity, debt) and what was actually
delivered in later quarters. Score management's guidance accuracy. Note shifts
in tone, newly introduced metrics, and metrics that quietly disappeared.
```

```text
5) VARIANT PERCEPTION + REVERSE DCF
State (a) the consensus view and what the current price implies: solve a
reverse DCF for the revenue growth and margin needed over 10 years at a
[12–13% INR / 9% USD] discount rate; (b) my variant view: [paste]; (c) the
specific catalyst/trigger and its timing; (d) whether the implied growth is
plausible against base rates (few firms sustain >20% growth for 10 years).
Decompose a 5-year scenario into EPS growth × P/E change (twin engine).
```

```text
6) STEELMAN THE BEAR / PRE-MORTEM
Act as a skeptical short-seller. It is 3 years from now and this position lost
60%. Write the most plausible story of why, using only public data. Test the
moat, customer concentration, capital allocation, governance, and valuation if
growth disappoints by 20–30%. Then list 5 measurable KILL CRITERIA that would
tell me early that this story is happening.
```

```text
7) QUESTIONS FOR MANAGEMENT / SCUTTLEBUTT
List 15 questions ranked by information value for management, and 10 for
channel checks (dealers, distributors, customers, ex-employees), that would
most change my estimate of [key value driver].
```

```text
8) THESIS TRACKER (quarterly)
Here is my thesis memo and kill criteria [paste]. Here are the new results,
concall and shareholding pattern [attach]. For each thesis pillar and kill
criterion: confirmed / weakened / broken, with citations. Has the variant
perception been priced in (P/E vs my target, consensus estimate revisions)?
Recommend: hold / add / trim / exit, with reasons — I will decide.
```

In Claude Code with the equity-research plugin, `/thesis` and `/catalysts` can maintain prompts 8 and 5 on a schedule, and `/screen` can seed idea generation. **The human sets sizing and makes the final decision.** Delegating order placement to an agent is exactly the overtrading failure that sank most Alpha Arena entrants.

body:
All figures in this section are single-source, from screener consolidated on 19 Nov 2026.

- **KFin Tech** (₹936, 45× P/E): OPM fell from 45% to 34–40% because of investment and acquisitions. Promoter General Atlantic sold down from 32.9% to 14.1%, and DIIs absorbed it (19% → 37.5%). There is no margin step-change. The price implies ~17% CAGR. Revisit if OPM gets back above 42%.
- **CAMS** (₹714, 35×): Best-in-class quality, ROCE 47%, CFO above PAT. But growth is ~10–15%, and FIIs fell from 57.6% to 45.6%. It is fairly priced at ~14% implied growth, not a multibagger.
- **Anand Rathi Wealth**: Mcap of ₹39k cr is outside the band. P/E 86×, and the Sep-26 quarter OPM dropped from 46% to 34%.
- **Nuvama**: Mcap ₹34k cr. Borrowings of ₹13.2k cr and persistently negative CFO make it a balance-sheet business.
- **UTI AMC**: A loss quarter in Mar-26 (−₹51 cr). Earnings are MTM-heavy and ROE is 10%.
- **CDSL** (59×) and **Angel One**: The F&O damage is already reflected in the numbers, and the Sep-26 quarters recovered. CDSL is too expensive. Angel One has ₹7.6k cr of debt and CFO of −₹4.1k cr.
- **Radico Khaitan**: The pattern proof (OPM 13% → 21%), but mcap is ₹62k cr and the price implies ~24% CAGR at 78×.
- **Tilaknagar**: The Imperial Blue acquisition took borrowings from ₹44 cr to ₹2,301 cr. There were loss quarters in Dec-25 and Mar-26, CFO of −₹445 cr, ROCE 11%, and debtor days of 198. It is a special situation, not a clean step-change.
- **Sula Vineyards**: OPM collapsed from 31% to 18%, ROCE is 8%, and FIIs went from 9.6% to 0.35%. A broken premiumisation story.
- **Piccadily Agro (Indri)**: The premiumisation brand is real, but the margin peaked (26–28% → 17–21%). Sep-26 PAT was −15% YoY, debt rose from ₹154 cr to ₹550 cr, debtor days from 32 to 89, and the ENA capex dilutes the mix. **Watchlist.**
- **Associated Alcohols**: Cheap at 14.5× and near its 52-week low, but Sep-26 OPM collapsed to 6.5% with no explained cause. **Watchlist** until the cause is known.
- **Globus Spirits**: ROCE 11% and erratic margins.
- **Jewellery (Senco, PN Gadgil, Thangamayil [standalone], Sky Gold)**: Gold-price inventory gains inflate margins and make P/Es look cheap (Senco 8.75×). CFO is deeply negative (Senco −₹789 cr, PNG −₹717 cr) and borrowings are ballooning. Sky Gold has the best growth (Sep-26 qtr PAT ₹129 cr vs ₹67 cr) but negative CFO every year. These are not mix stories, and they reverse if gold corrects.
- **Metro Brands**: P/E 54, OPM flat at 30%, FIIs falling. No step-change.
- **Campus** (standalone; the consolidated page is stale at 2022): OPM flat at 13–19%, P/E 44.
- **Mrs Bectors**: Steady 13% OPM, P/E 42, FIIs 15.6% → 6.0%.
- **V2 Retail**: Growth is debt-funded (₹525 cr → ₹1,379 cr) and FY26 CFO was −₹103 cr.
- **Jyothy Labs**: Screener consolidated data stops at Mar-25, so it could not be verified. Excluded.
- **Devyani**: P/E 1,304× and ROCE 4.75%. The QSR recovery has not shown up.

title: buffett_lynch › Gaps

body:
- Amazon fell about 94% (some sources say 95%) from December 1999 to late 2001, from roughly $113 to $6, and took about a decade to regain the peak. Long-term holders still got rich. — [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2018/12/18/dotcom-bubble-amazon-stock-lost-more-than-90percent-long-term-investors-still-got-rich.html); [Benzinga (Bezos: "the stock is not the company")](https://benzinga.com/tech/25/05/45426247/jeff-bezos-once-watched-amazons-stock-collapse-from-113-to-6-but-held-on-to-the-belief-that-the-stock-is-not-the-company-heres-how-he-weathered-that-st)
- Apple, Microsoft, and Nvidia each had drawdowns of more than 80%, and most stocks fall more than 50% at some point. — [Irish Times](https://www.irishtimes.com/your-money/2025/06/17/the-agony-and-the-equity-most-stocks-fall-more-than-50-at-some-point). Netflix fell 60% or more four times, twice by about 90%. — [A Wealth of Common Sense](https://awealthofcommonsense.com/2021/03/owning-the-best-stocks-is-hard/)
- Mauboussin (Consilient Observer, "Drawdowns and Recoveries"): the top wealth creators (Apple, Microsoft, NVIDIA, Alphabet, Amazon, ExxonMobil) added $17.1tn, but buying and holding them meant enduring large drawdowns. — [Eaton Vance / Mauboussin PDF](https://www.eatonvance.com/content/dam/im/assets/publication/thought-leadership/consilient-observer/article_drawdownsandrecoveries.pdf)
- Dot-com tech IPOs had a median terminal drawdown of −85%, and the survivors produced some of history's highest returns. This is survivorship again: most never recovered. — [Lambda Finance](https://www.lambdafin.com/articles/tech-ipo-drawdown-history)
- **MYTH: the Fidelity "dead or forgot" study.** It traces to James O'Shaughnessy recounting it on Barry Ritholtz's Bloomberg radio show. No original Fidelity research has been located, and commentators call it "folklore". — [Wood Gundy (CIBC)](https://woodgundyadvisors.cibc.com/david-ricciardelli/blog/3073570-Yes-the-investors-with-the-best-returns-were-dead/); [Dividend Growth Investor](https://dividendgrowthinvestor.com/2021/01/the-best-investors-in-world-are-dead.html); [Motley Fool discussion](https://discussion.fool.com/t/best-investing-strategy/34550). The lesson it is meant to illustrate is supported by real data: Barber & Odean and Morningstar, in Section 3.
